$comment: Registered exceptions to constitution VII's stage-layer rule, enforced by
and again at release-dispatch time from release.yml's Gate 1b.
A workflow_call-only stage is the PUBLISHED CONTRACT: it owns no trigger
and reads no ambient repository state. Every deviation lives here, in the
open, with a reason and either an OPEN tracking issue or a permanent
marker (Gate 124, verify-waiver-citations.py) -- never as a name missing from a
list, and never as a code comment alone. watchdog.yml's exception used to
be expressed by NOT APPEARING in release.yml's brace expansion, while its
own comment called itself 'release.yml Gate 1b's documented vars.*-read
exception' and release.yml never mentioned the watchdog (#149).
Every entry is STALE-CHECKED in both directions. A pattern that matches
nothing fails the gate, so a waiver cannot outlive its reason. A `count`
that no longer matches fails the gate, so a waived deviation can neither
grow nor quietly widen past the deviation it covers. Changing a count is
therefore a deliberate, reviewed act -- which is the point: at v2.2.0
every stage the old gate DID cover read vars.* exactly zero times, so a
waiver should feel uncomfortable to hold.

waivers.permanent_reason: The watchdog is a supervisor that reads repository variables by design; the count guards against growth.
waivers.reason: The watchdog is a supervisor: it has to locate the adopter's branches and durable stores and read its own tuning knobs, so it reads repository variables where every other stage takes inputs. Each added read is a deliberate, reviewed change to `count` -- a twenty-third read fails this gate on the pull request that introduces it. Removing the reads would mean turning them into workflow_call inputs, a breaking change reserved for a future major.
